item.title: 2027: Okorocha ‘never contested’ Imo West primary – Uzodimma’s aide
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA The Deputy Chief of Staff to Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, Chief Enyinna Onuegbu, has said former Governor Rochas Okorocha never took part in the All Progressives Congress APC primary for Imo West Senatorial District, which a Federal High Court in Abuja has now ruled he won. Read Also: Orlu Senatorial Seat: War in Imo as Okorocha battles Uzodimma Onuegbu, a lawyer, spoke on Friday evening on Arise News, monitored in Abuja, in a right of reply to Okorocha, who appeared on the same programme about 24 hours earlier. “Imo APC people never saw Okorocha as an aspirant and he didn’t participate and was not even physically present in Imo State anywhere at any level. Any briefing of stakeholders, any briefing of delegates, any event conducted prior to that primaries, Senator Okorocha was not physically present,” Onuegbu sai He asked at what stage Okorocha addressed party members as an aspirant. “At what stage did he consult? At what stage has he been able to provide evidence of I have been declared winner at any level, ward, LGA or state?” he asked. Onuegbu said the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the committee that conducted the primary both rejected the documents Okorocha relied on before the court. “When the court, in its own documentation, the processes filed in court, showed that both INEC, the authority that supervised, APC committee that conducted, all denied the documents His Excellency Rochas Okorocha relied on. Before the court, they all denied them as forgeries, fictitious, and totally fabricated,” he said. According to him, the court “chose to rely on what applicant filed without averting its mind to the need to resolve the conflict in the documentation brought by both parties.” Onuegbu argued that where documents conflict in an originating summons, “the law requires the court to resolve the conflict by oral evidence of witnesses.” In his words, “What the law requires the court to do is to call evidence of witnesses so that they can be put to cross-examination.” He added that the Supreme Court had held that “when forgeries are alleged, what the court is left to do is to put the parties to the witness box.” Asked whether Uzodimma’s side had been denied the chance to present its own documents, Onuegbu said that was not the point. “He put forward documents and we put documents that showed that the authority that did the work disputed what he put. So this contradiction can only be resolved” by hearing witnesses, he said. He rejected Okorocha’s reference to “Hope’s document,” saying the governor did not run the exercise. “Governor Hope Uzodimma was not the one who conducted the primaries. He was an aspirant like he was. Governor Hope Uzodimma was not the person who declared the result,” he said. item.title: Orlu Senatorial Seat: War in Imo as Okorocha battles Uzodimma
item.description: •Court grants Okorocha ticket, 12 Chairmen back go vernor By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA The fight over who flies the All Progressives Congress (APC) flag in Imo West Senatorial District has turned into open war, with the party’s 12 local government chairmen in the zone rejecting a court judgment that handed the ticket to former Governor Rochas Okorocha and insisting that Governor Hope Uzodimma remains the candidate. Read Also: Tinubu has broken Imo’s shackles — Okorocha hails court judgment The chairmen made their stand known on Friday at a press conference in Owerri, a day after a Federal High Court in Abuja sacked Uzodimma as the party’s candidate for the January 16, 2027 Senate election. State APC chairman, Austin Onyedebelu spoke on behalf of the Chairmen. Said he: “We reject this judgment in its entirety because it is an undisguised travesty of justice. It is a political robbery clothed in legal robes, the latest instalment of a satanic scheme hatched by Abuja politicians against the South-East,” the chairmen declared. Justice Obiora Egwuatu ruled on Thursday that Okorocha, and not the governor, won the party’s May 18 primary for the district. He held that Okorocha had produced “sufficient evidence” that he won the exercise, which was monitored by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Court order The court ordered the APC to forward Okorocha’s name to INEC and directed the commission to publish him as the party’s validly nominated candidate. It also barred Uzodimma from presenting himself as the APC candidate in the election. The chairmen said they were in the field on May 18, 2026, when the primary was held, and that Okorocha scored only 1,098 votes against about 230,000 for Uzodimma, who was declared winner in the presence of INEC staff. “For the avoidance of doubt, we NEVER VOTED FOR ROCHAS OKOROCHA,” Onyedebelu said. “This legal somersault orchestrated by enemies of Ndigbo was obviously procured not only to destabilise Orlu zone but to consolidate the war of attrition by some Nigerians to politically hold down the south east.” They said Okorocha never used the window provided by the party to petition its appeal panel over any irregularity, only to go to court and be handed victory. The chairmen pointed to what they called wild celebrations by Okorocha since Thursday and his remarks that he got help from higher quarters outside the court. In their view, this showed a conspiracy to shut Ndigbo out of political relevance. item.title: ‘Northern leaders begged Tinubu to support Buhari, promised to return power after eight years’ – APC chieftain
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, APC, and former House of Representative member representing Birnin-Kudu/ Buji in Jigawa State, Engr. Magaji Da’u Aliyu, has claimed that Northern political leaders begged President Bola Tinubu to support former President Muhammadu Buhari’s presidential ambition and promised to return power to his side after eight years. ‎Aliyu, who is also the Deputy Campaign Director of the North for Tinubu Support Group, disclosed this while addressing supporters in Birnin Kudu. ‎He said the North has no justification for opposing Tinubu’s re-election in the 2027 general election, insisting that the region must honour the political agreement allegedly reached before Buhari became president in 2015. ‎ ‎According to him, Buhari had contested the presidential election three times without success before Northern political leaders approached Tinubu in Lagos to seek his support. ‎ ‎”Buhari contested the presidential election three times and lost. We then went to Lagos to beg Tinubu to support Buhari’s presidential ambition,” he said. ‎ ‎”He agreed to support us on the understanding that after Buhari’s eight years in office, power would return to his side, and we accepted the agreement.” ‎ ‎Aliyu maintained that supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 is a matter of honouring the promise made to him, stressing that Northerners have no reason to abandon the agreement. ‎ ‎”For every Northerner, fulfilling that agreement is mandatory. We have no reason not to honour the agreement we entered into,” he said. ‎ ‎The APC chieftain pledged that members of the Northern Tinubu Support Group would commit their resources towards ensuring the President’s victory in the next presidential election. ‎ ‎”On our part, we will support Tinubu’s re-election bid with our lives and wealth to ensure that we fulfil the promise we made,” he added. ‎ ‎Speaking on insecurity, Aliyu also defended President Tinubu against criticism over the country’s security challenges. ‎ ‎He argued that no human being has absolute power to guarantee security, insisting that only God can provide lasting peace and stability. ‎ ‎”Let us stop the blame game. Only God has the power to provide security. We should seek His forgiveness, and He will grant us peace and stability,” he said. item.title: Drunk barber allegedly stabs man to death in Jigawa
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested a 29-year-old barber, Emmanuel Olatonok, for allegedly stabbing a 32-year-old man, Ibrahim Shago, to death while reportedly under the influence of alcohol. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Shiisu Lawan Adam, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists. The incident occurred on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at about 5:45 p.m. in the Rafin Sanyi area of Dutse Local Government Area. According to the police spokesperson, the suspect, who reportedly worked as a barber at a hotel in Dutse, allegedly stabbed the victim in the neck with a knife following an argument. He added that the suspect was allegedly under the influence of alcohol at the time of the incident. “The suspect, a barber reportedly working at a popular hotel in Dutse, allegedly stabbed the victim in the neck with a knife following an argument,” he said. Adam explained that the victim, a resident of Karnaya town, was immediately rushed to a hospital for medical attention but was later confirmed dead by a medical doctor. He said the incident triggered tension in the area as some angry youths gathered at the scene and attempted to vandalise the hotel. However, police operatives from Dutse Division quickly intervened and brought the situation under control, preventing further violence and destruction of property. The police spokesperson confirmed that the suspect is currently in custody, while investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the killing. He added that the suspect would be charged to court upon the conclusion of the investigation. item.title: 21 cars affected as fire engulfs Lagos mechanic workshop
item.description: By Evelyn Usman A mechanic workshop went up in flames in the early hours of yesterday at Isheri-Idimu, Alimosho Local Government Area of Lagos State, with 21 vehicles reportedly affected. The fire, which broke out at about 3:05am on Oladunni Street, beside Eternal Filling Station, reportedly threatened to spread to the adjoining petrol station, raising fears of a possible major disaster, according to eyewitnesses. However, the swift intervention of emergency responders reportedly prevented the inferno from spreading to the filling station and nearby buildings. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) said its Dolphin Response Team, stationed at Igando, was immediately activated following a distress call. The Permanent Secretary of LASEMA, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, said: “Upon arrival, responders discovered that the fire had engulfed a mechanical workshop where several exotic vehicles were parked, in close proximity to a petroleum filling station. Through the prompt, professional and coordinated intervention of the LASEMA Response Team and the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, supported by the Lagos Neighbourhood Safety Corps and the Nigeria Police Force, the inferno was prevented from spreading to the filling station and surrounding structures, thereby averting what could have been a major disaster. “The fire has been completely extinguished and damping-down operations concluded. Preliminary assessment indicates that about twenty-one (21) exotic vehicles were affected, with a section of a nearby building sustaining minor damage. “Importantly, no loss of life and no injury were recorded. “The Lagos State Government, through LASEMA, reiterates its commitment to the protection of lives and property across the state. The agency commends the bravery and diligence of all responders whose swift action ensured that the incident was brought under control without casualties. “Members of the public are enjoined to continue to prioritise safety measures, particularly in workshops and environments where inflammable materials are handled, and to promptly alert emergency services through the toll-free emergency numbers 767 and 112 in the event of any emergency,” he said. item.title: Can Tinubu’s education reforms rescue a generation? – Inside Alausa’s ambitious agenda
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja With nearly 46 million children reportedly captured in a new education data system, almost 250,000 Nigerians undergoing technical skills training and the government claiming to have returned one million out-of-school children to classrooms, the Tinubu administration is making an ambitious case for an education turnaround. But can impressive figures translate into lasting educational transformation? For decades, Nigeria’s education crisis has been defined by millions of children outside classrooms, overcrowded schools, inadequate facilities, poorly equipped laboratories, frustrated teachers and graduates struggling to find employment despite their qualifications Now, in the office of the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, a digital dashboard is offering a different picture–one the minister says provides an unprecedented opportunity to monitor schools, track enrolment, identify infrastructure gaps and examine the distribution of teachers and pupils nationwide. With a few clicks, Alausa explained, officials can drill down into individual schools to examine enrollment figures, the number of girls, available facilities and teaching personnel. For a country long challenged by fragmented education statistics, this represents a potentially significant shift. But the real test of Nigeria’s education reforms is not how impressive the dashboard appears in Abuja. It is whether the technology delivers better classrooms, competent teachers, improved learning outcomes and greater opportunities for millions of children. That is the central question confronting Alausa as he presents President Bola Tinubu’s education reforms as the beginning of a measurable turnaround. Alausa Speaking while receiving notification of his selection for Vanguard’s Public Sector Icon of the Year award, the minister outlined six priority areas: technical and vocational education and training, science and technology education, reducing the out-of-school population, girls’ education, data and digitalisation, and improving educational quality and teacher effectiveness. Together, these priorities seek to address a fundamental contradiction in Nigerian education: expanding access without guaranteeing learning, producing graduates without adequate practical skills and increasing enrolment without providing sufficient infrastructure. With Nigeria’s population estimated at approximately 220 million and a youthful demographic, Alausa argued that education reform was imperative. The challenge is to turn this demographic advantage into economic productivity rather than allow it to deepen unemployment, inequality and insecurity Perhaps the most consequential element of Alausa’s presentation was the ministry’s cloud-based education dashboard, which he said captures information on nearly 46 million children. item.title: To save Esan language from extinction, I’ll do anything – Dr. Mabel Imooje
item.description: By Fred Iwenjora Dr. Mabel Imooje holds a doctorate degree in linguistics from Bayero University, Kano. The staff of National Institute for Hospitality and Tourism, Kano is making name as an advocate for the survival of Esan Language seen by many researches as one of the indigenous languages set to go extinct if drastic measures are not taken. Imooje travels across Nigeria at her spare time meeting Esan speaking people, giving them reasons to strive to sustain the language. The associate member of Nigerian Institute of Translators and Interpreters. (NITI) tells FRED IWENJORA the inspiration behind this arduous advocacy. She also discusses the hurdles as well as triumphs so far. “My inspiration comes from my passion for Esan language. The language is so very hard wired in my brain that no one needs ask where I come from whenever I speak. Any Nigerian or Edo state native does not need to ask of my tribe before he/she with affirmation will say, ‘you are an Esan’. “My accent is so strong in my speech, and I feel it’s impact should be used in improving language instruction, develop teaching materials and create learning resources for our dear language. Have you documented these in a book? Not yet but it is in the pipeline. I have been fascinated by languages and always wished to speak about theories and workings of indigenous languages. What course of study prepared you for this? I first started with an NCE in English/Social Studies. Later, I got a degree and a master’s in English before switching to linguistics at doctorate level. I did this to really understand how indigenous languages work and of course with special interest in Esan language. I will also say here that I love my language and wanted it documented from my own point of view. On why she went local rather than beginning from abroad with French, Spanish, Italian or even Mandarin, she hinted that “Going local is to encourage indigenous languages to pop up amongst the foreign languages that you just mentioned. No one watches his or her inheritance erode through wreckless abandonments. I decided to go local to save my language from extinction. Esan is both a people and a language spoken in five local government areas in the Edo Central Senatorial district. It is one of the endangered languages of the world. It should be noted that several factors cause language endangerment. These include diminishing number of the native speakers, age, failure to use the language by the children, negative attitude of the native speaker towards the language, rural – urban shift and so on, just to mention but a few. Therefore, my going local is to lend my voice to other crusaders to say ‘no’ to extinction of indigenous languages. You mean we shouldn’t chase foreign languages? I did not mean that. Proficiency in English and any other foreign languages is good for socio-economic mobility and national integration but it can also lead to marginalisation of indigenous languages. item.title: 46-yr-old businessman commits suicide, leaves video message for family
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure A 46-year-old businessman, Akinbolusere Kayode, has reportedly died by suicide in Ondo Town, Ondo State. Sources said he took his life in his office near BOVAS Petrol Station in Igba Town at about 3 p.m. on Thursday. Two empty bottles suspected to have contained poisonous substance were recovered by police detectives attached to the Bolorunduro Division who visited the scene. According to sources, the deceased recorded a video in which he spoke about his business challenges, humble beginnings, and relationship with his wife, whom he praised for standing by him throughout his struggles. He also repeatedly stated that no one pressured him into deciding to transfer his properties to his wife and three children. The state Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, confirmed the incident. Abayomi said the two empty bottles suspected to have contained Sniper insecticide were recovered from a nearby bush during the police investigation. He added that preliminary findings indicated that the deceased recorded a video before his death in which he lamented the hardships he faced in life. The video has since circulated widely on social media. His remains were evacuated and deposited at the State Hospital morgue for preservation and further examination. Police said no signs of foul play or visible injuries were observed on the body during the initial examination. The Commissioner of Police in the state, Felix Ohagwu, has ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident to determine the actual cause of death. Ohagwu urged members of the public to refrain from speculation and allow investigators to carry out their work. He also advised individuals experiencing emotional distress, marital difficulties, or other personal challenges to seek timely support and assistance rather than resorting to actions that could endanger their lives. item.title: 2027: Obi not a threat in Lagos; we’ve corrected 2023 mistakes — APC
item.description: Chieftains of the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Lagos State said on Thursday that the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr. Peter Obi, is not a threat in the state, as the mistake of 2023, when Obi won the presidential election in the state, has been corrected. The APC stalwarts stated this while fielding questions from journalists at the launch of the political movement established by the daughter of President Bola Tinubu and Iyaloja General of Nigeria, Dr. Mujidat Folasade Tinubu-Ojo, in Abuja. The movement, named the Iyaloja General Movement (IGM), is to mobilise votes for President Tinubu’s re-election in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. The Lagos State Director-General of the movement, Barrister Adejumbo Omofumilewa, said the inauguration served as a mini-rally in support of Tinubu ahead of the 2027 elections. Omofumilewa expressed confidence that the APC would perform better in Lagos State in the next presidential election, saying the party had addressed the factors that led to its loss in the state during the 2023 presidential poll. He attributed the outcome of the previous election to the party’s failure to adequately assess the political situation in Lagos, describing the experience as a betrayal. “What happened in 2023 that made our candidate lose the presidential election in Lagos State has already been taken care of, because now, everybody is following him,” he said. Omofumilewa also dismissed the prospect of opposition parties posing a serious challenge to the APC in Lagos, insisting that the ruling party had a strong presence across the state. “Obi is not a threat, neither is any party a threat in Lagos State. We are in charge,” he said, adding that the party was politically and organisationally positioned to secure victory in 2027. On his part, the Director-General of IGM, Dr. Nasiru Ladan, said the movement had already attracted over 2,500 support groups, with more organisations expressing interest. Ladan said the groups had been integrated into the movement’s structure and that the organisation was building a database of supporters across states and local government areas. “We have just started; it has been launched today, and we have machinery in motion in all the states, local governments, up to the ward level,” he said. He explained that the movement’s grassroots strategy was designed to translate its organisational structure into votes for the APC in 2027. According to him, the movement plans to deploy 10 facilitators to each polling unit, with each facilitator expected to mobilise 100 voters. He said the initiative was expected to help the movement achieve its target of 10 million votes, although he did not provide a breakdown of how the target would be measured or independently verified. item.title: 2027: How we will curb election violence — INEC
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, has unveiled an intelligence-led security framework to curb violence ahead of the 2027 General Election, vowing to hunt down anyone who threatens its ad-hoc staff, National Youth Service Corps NYSC members or permanent personnel. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this in Gombe on Tuesday while declaring open the North-East Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment for the 2027 General Election. The Commission in its daily bulletin said it was shifting from reactive, election-day deployments to a framework designed to protect voters, personnel and electoral materials before any ballot paper is moved. INEC said its collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC, the Department of State Services DSS, the Armed Forces and other paramilitary agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security ICCES has, according to him, been fundamentally restructured. The new framework, which the Commission terms the “ICCES Tentacle,” extends inter-agency security coordination from national and state headquarters directly down to the most remote Local Government Areas and Registration Area Centres. Amupitan told the gathering that no election, however well planned administratively, could be deemed credible if voters, election personnel and observers operate under physical threat or fear of violence. He explained that the framework rests on three pillars, the first being “Map and Mitigate.” Under it, the Commission will use Electoral Risk Management (ERM) tools to identify security flashpoints, seasonal threat factors and local vulnerabilities early, so that security agencies can deploy proactive measures long before ballot papers arrive. The second pillar, “Ensure Safety,” provides a protective umbrella over all electoral personnel, technological assets, including Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and server infrastructure, and, most importantly, the voter. The third pillar, “Guarantee Access,” is aimed at ensuring that each of the 176,846 polling units nationwide remains a safe, peaceful and dignified space for the exercise of democratic rights, regardless of geographical remoteness or historical security challenges. According to him, the collaboration among the agencies had already produced concrete results. He disclosed that joint operations led by the DSS recently uncovered a covert plot by criminal kingpins targeting the Commission’s ad-hoc staff and Youth Corps members. item.title: Niger Illegal Miners: Detainees drank urine, sweat in NSCDC cell before 33 died – Report
item.description: Details have emerged of how alleged illegal miners held in a cell at the Niger State Command of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) drank urine or sweat because they had no access to drinking water before 33 of them died. Read Also: Full List: Names of 37 miners who died in NSCDC custody In a report submitted by the Independent Investigation Committee, constituted by the Federal Ministry of Interior to investigate the deaths, it was discovered that the male cell had no running water and its toilet was not functioning. The report quoted survivors as describing how they experienced extreme heat, dehydration and overcrowding, while they were unable to move freely inside the approximately 12-square-metre cell. The Jonathan Kure-led 10-member committee authenticated 33 deaths occuring inside the male cell between 8 p.m. on 16 September and 7 a.m. the following day 17 September. The committee said the detainees had no drinking water, while officers ignored warnings about overcrowding and the risk of suffocation. According to the copy of the report obtained by PREMIUM TIMES, the deceased persons included 14 minors. The report, which painted a deplorable, harsh condition of the cell, stated that there were 41 survivors. It found that about 50 male detainees, including children, were confined in the cell, which had a solid metal door and inadequate ventilation. “The Committee finds that officers responsible for the cells failed to reduce the overcrowding, ignored prolonged cries and banging of the cell door and wall and did not provide emergency help,” the report said. Under the dehumanising condition of the male cell, the report said, there was “no water” and “toilet not functional”. It added that “detainees drank urine or sweat.” The situation in the female cell was barely better. The report said there was also “no drinking water” there, except from relatives. The toilet was also “non-functional but usable with fetched water,” according to the report. It added that relatives were prevented from bringing food to detainees on Wednesday, 16 September, the committee said. Warnings ignored The committee found that medical personnel had warned officers about the danger posed by the overcrowded cell before the deaths. Mariam Nelson, an NSCDC medical unit personnel, told the committee that she cautioned the cell guards, Usman Ndamaka and Hassan Mohammed, on the evening of 16 September that the overcrowding could cause suffocation. She said she advised them to leave the metal door unlocked to improve ventilation, but they ignored her warning. The report said detainees began experiencing symptoms, including eye irritation, burning throats, difficulty breathing, excessive sweating and intense thirst, from around 7:15 p.m. on 16 September. They subsequently began shouting for help and pleading for water. An armoury guard, Ahmed Abubakar Wushishi, told the committee that he heard persistent banging and screams from the cell between 1 a.m. and 2 a.m.

item.title: Pharmacists warn against patronising street medicine vendors
item.description: •Say adulterated drugs can cause collapse of health sector By James Ogunnaike; Shina Abubakar & Deola Badru Pharmacists have warned Nigerians against patronising street medicine vendors following the growing threat posed by fake and counterfeit medicines in the country. Read Also: Deadly goods on sale: How fake products damage organs, destroy lives Speaking on the prevalence of counterfeit and substandard medicines in the country, they stressed that the problem poses serious risks to public health, including treatment failure, toxic reactions and potential damage to vital organs such as the liver and kidneys. They therefore called for stricter monitoring of medicines imported into the country, improved regulation of drug manufacturing and distribution and greater public awareness of the dangers associated with purchasing medicines from unauthorised sources. According to Pharm. Franklin Uzoezie: “Fake drugs, also known as counterfeit medicines, are products that do not meet the required standards or do not contain what they claim to contain. This could involve the active ingredient, the strength or dosage, or even the packaging. In some cases, a medicine may claim to contain a particular drug but contain none of it. In other instances, it may contain the drug but not in the correct quantity or strength. All these are examples of counterfeit or substandard medicines. The increasing circulation of fake and substandard medicines in Nigeria has become a major public health concern “The truth is that even healthcare professionals may find it difficult to distinguish between fake and genuine medicines just by looking at them. Their appearance, packaging and other features may be almost identical. In some cases, counterfeit products may even look better than the original medicines. Simply examining a medicine with the naked eye may not be enough to determine whether it is genuine or counterfeit. Appropriate laboratory analysis may be required to establish its composition and quality “When a medicine is counterfeit or substandard, it may contain the wrong ingredients, an incorrect quantity of the active ingredient, or potentially harmful substances. This can make the product ineffective or toxic to the body. The most important precaution is to know where you obtain your medicines. We often advise patients and members of the public not to buy medicines from just any place where they are being sold. Nigerians must purchase their medicines from licensed pharmacies and other legally authorised medicine outlets. “As patients and members of the public, we should not choose where to buy medicines solely because a seller offers a lower price or is conveniently located. We must prioritise the safety, quality and authenticity of the medicines we use. Purchasing medicines from approved sources, strengthening regulatory oversight and improving public awareness would help reduce the risk of exposure to counterfeit and substandard products”. item.title: Deadly goods on sale: How fake products damage organs, destroy lives
item.description: *Everyday purchases now turn to health hazards *Patients end up paying twice for treatment —Adefunke Adeniyi *Counterfeit drugs damage kidneys, liver — Amarachukwu Enahoro *Adulterated drugs can cause collapse of health sector — Pharmacists warn By Chioma Obinna It is an understatement to say that Nigeria is currently battling a health crisis. Virtually every product, drug, food or drink is being counterfeited in the country and the consequence is fatal. Toddlers are no longer safe because counterfeit baby foods are everywhere. Parents now need to exercise caution in the choice of biscuits to give to their children as some biscuits have been discovered to contain toxic. A tablet swallowed to cure malaria could end up damaging the kidneys or liver while a bottle of drink bought to quench thirst could expose the consumer to dangerous substances. Similarly, cooking oil packaged under a trusted brand could contain ingredients far removed from what the label promises. For millions of Nigerians, the growing menace of fake and substandard products has turned everyday purchases into a potentially deadly gamble, with consequences ranging from failed treatment and organ damage to disability and death. The scale of the threat is underscored by the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), which reported destroying unsafe, falsified and non-compliant regulated products worth ₦22.73 billion between January and August 2026. Yet, beyond the billions of naira in seized and destroyed goods lies a more disturbing reality: the human cost of a trade that preys on consumers, undermines medical treatment, drains family resources and puts lives at risk. Health experts have therefore raised the alarm that harmful substances in counterfeit medicines, drinks and food products can damage vital organs. The question now is no longer just how much Nigeria is losing to fake products, but how many lives are being put in danger. When the medicine fails The danger is particularly serious when counterfeit or substandard medicines are used to treat common illnesses such as malaria. A patient experiencing fever and body aches may buy an antimalarial, take it as directed and expect to recover. But a medicine containing insufficient active ingredients, no effective ingredient or an inappropriate substance may fail to treat the illness, allowing the patient’s condition to worsen. Dr Amarachukwu Enahoro, a medical doctor and public health physician at Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH), said counterfeit medicines could defeat the very purpose for which they were purchased. “The consequence for that person might be that the main purpose for which this medicine was put, which is to treat malaria, will not be achieved,” she said. “The second implication is that it can now cause damage. item.title: Masussuka: Life, preaching, death
item.description: The murder of Katsina-based Islamic cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka, has stirred emotions and sparked conversations around the life and times of a popular preacher seen through different lenses. To his army of followers, he embodied peace, dignity and tolerance for religious differences. To his critics, he was a controversial scholar whose religious ideology and preaching were questionable. Masussuka was shot dead alongside his associate, Adamu Abubakar, on Monday evening in front of his house at Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, in an attack claimed by the extremist group, Ansaru. Amnesty International has called on the Nigerian government to conduct a thorough investigation into the killing and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice. Masussuka: We reject his ideology but condemn his killing – JIBWIS Imam Masussuka’s preaching, killing contrary to Islamic laws – Sheikh Maraya The 47-year-old cleric subscribed to and preached Quranic teachings, but, to greater extent, disregarded Hadith, the sayings and practices of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) – a stance that placed him at variance with his critics. He alleged that a lot of Hadiths being attributed to the Prophet were not from him, saying they were concocted by some people out of mischief. Masussuka reportedly began preaching at the tender age of 13 and rose to prominence with the advent of social media, through which he established himself as one of the most vocal clerics among the Qur’aniyun Islamic sect. Through his active social media platforms, his preaching gained more recognition, increasingly attracting attention from other sects with different ideologies. Masussuka’s increased visibility drew controversies around his ideology. One major controversy surrounding Masussuka’s teachings and ideology revolved around his rejection of certain Hadith traditions as authorities and forms of religious practice. According to other sects, his doctrine that only the Qur’an serves as the gateway to religious practice goes contrary to a larger belief that both the Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet are central sources of Islamic guidance. Disagreements over his ideology became more pronounced and his teachings were challenged on several occasions. Though disagreement on the interpretation and authority of Hadith has long existed among Muslim scholars, Masussuka’s unique stance on the matter placed him at odds with scholars who considered his teachings inconsistent with established Islamic traditions. Amid growing scrutiny of his preaching, the Katsina State Government, on November 18, 2025, announced that Masussuka would be required to defend his teachings before a committee of Islamic scholars established based on the several calls. The meeting, however, didn’t see the light of day due to undisclosed circumstances, as he continued to challenge other sects that go against his ideologies. item.title: Parallel campaigns within APC
item.description: While the All Progressives Congress (APC) officially kicked off its presidential campaign last week, a major hindrance to its effective spread in all the geopolitical zones and states in the country has remained the lack of synergy in many states. Weekend Trust checks revealed that there are many states where leaders of the party claiming to work for the reelection of its presidential candidate, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, prefer to work in isolated camps, without as much as involving other leaders in its operations. This, our correspondent learnt, is due to unresolved leadership disputes, personality clashes and the bid outdo each other to prove the one with the bigger political worth. The intensity, however, varies in degree from state to state, with some openly defying each other, while some put up a façade of working together, but beneath the surface are trying to undermine each other’s efforts. Masussuka: Life, preaching, death Nigeria’s drug battle Investigations reveal that in states where the governors joined the APC only after winning elections, the process of integrating the party structure on ground has not been concluded, leading to suspicion between those who moved the governors and those they met on ground. In states like Plateau, Taraba, Adamawa and Kano, there are still vestiges of animosity between the two major camps of the defecting governors and those they met on ground. In states like Anambra and Osun, where the governors are members of other parties but have been integrated into the APC presidential campaign council, the preexisting party structures there have shown that they are not comfortable with the arrangement. States like Benue, Ondo, Katsina, Zamfara have shown that the contending forces are not aligned to work together for the reelection bid of its presidential candidate due to unrestrained rivalries between the governors and other powerful figures from the party in their states, who have the ears of Abuja. Our correspondents capture what is going on in some of the states. Masari yet to attend Radda’s campaign rallies in Katsina As the Katsina State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) begins its 2027 re-election campaign, the Special Adviser to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Political and Other Matters, Alhaji Ibrahim Kabir Masari, is yet to attend any of the party’s major campaign activities in the state. Masari, who is considered one of the influential APC figures in Katsina, was absent during the inauguration of the Dikko/Tinubu Campaign Council by Governor Dikko Umaru Radda. He was also missing at the official flag-off of the campaign in Funtua Local Government Area. However, rather than joining the governor at the public campaign events, Masari is said to have intensified separate political consultations within and outside Katsina State ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Nigeria’s drug battle
item.description: Despite massive seizures, arrest of Nigerians and foreign nationals, prosecution and dismantling of clandestine methamphetamine laboratories linked to international criminal networks by the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), among others, drug trafficking remains a major challenge in Nigeria. From industrial-scale drug production to cocaine couriers and cross-border syndicates, the persistence of the illicit trade raises questions about the sophistication of criminal networks and the factors sustaining the business. The growing drug problem has continued to impact negatively on the health and general wellbeing of many Nigerians, especially the youth population. Many families and households note that they are going through a lot of trauma and pains in the management and rehabilitation of their children and loved ones who have become victims of drug addiction. Masussuka: Life, preaching, death Parallel campaigns within APC According to data from the NDLEA, over the last five years, a total of 96,157 suspects, including 250 drug barons, have been arrested; 15, 833, 856.3kgs of illicit drug seized with 2,099.96 hectares of cannabis farms destroyed. Within the same period, the agency secured 18,691 convictions while 54, 517 were counselled and rehabilitated. Between January 2026 and September 2026 alone, data showed that 18,290 arrests have been made with illicit drug seizures of 698,488.76kgs while 81.69 hectares of cannabis farms have been destroyed across the country. Within the same period, a total of 2,568 convictions were recorded while 5,681 were counselled and rehabilitated. The agency has also recorded the dismantling of four industrial meth laboratories across four states in recent months. Besides the destructions of meth laboratories, international drug traffickers, including those from South Africa and other parts of the world, have also been arrested in recent months, with some already facing prosecution. The agency also announced drug recoveries across several states, including Lagos, Kano, Bauchi, Niger, Edo, Ondo, Taraba, Oyo and Delta, anong others. Notwithstanding the massive seizures, arrests, convictions and destruction of illicit drugs by the agency, the drug trafficking challenge remains potent, with experts saying that Nigeria is not just a transit route for illicit drug but also evolving as a production hub. In this report, Weekend Trust examines some of the factors making Nigeria a drug trafficking destination and production hub, impacts on drug users and abusers, nexus between drug trafficking and insecurity, and the way forward. item.title: Oyemade urges Christians to seek divine direction
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Senior Pastor and Founder of Covenant Nations, Lagos, Pastor Poju Oyemade, has urged Christians to seek divine wisdom and revelation to discern God’s direction, saying situations that appear hopeless could become opportunities for victory through divine intervention. Oyemade gave the admonition while ministering at the ongoing 22nd International Prophetic Prayer Conference organised by the Throneroom Trust Ministry in Kafanchan, Kaduna State. Speaking on seven principles of prevailing prayer, which he said could help believers position themselves for the move of the Holy Spirit, the cleric maintained that God could bring victory out of situations people consider hopeless. “God is a God who commanded light to shine out of darkness and brings victory out of what you consider as defeat,” he said. Drawing from the Book of Ephesians, Oyemade referenced Apostle Paul’s prayer that God, the Father of Jesus Christ, would give believers the spirit of wisdom and revelation and enlighten the eyes of their understanding. He explained that God’s mercy manifests in different ways, noting that one of its significant expressions was opening the eyes of believers to see beyond their immediate circumstances. According to him, situations perceived as darkness could contain opportunities for divine intervention if believers were able to discern what God was doing. He urged Christians to embrace the prophetic dimension of their relationship with God, explaining that the way God intervened in their lives at one time might differ from how He chose to act at another. Oyemade also cautioned believers against concluding that a situation was hopeless when they encountered what appeared to be a dead end, urging them instead to seek God’s guidance to recognise the opportunities He had already provided. In a related development, the Vision Pioneer of Throneroom Trust Ministry, Kafanchan, Apostle Dr Emmanuel Nuhu Kure, called on Christian traditional rulers to build a legacy of faith and establish a lasting foundation for the work of Christ through their successors. Kure made the call during a special session dedicated to the rededication and prayers for traditional rulers and the land. He urged the traditional leaders to ensure that their reigns laid a foundation for the continued advancement of God’s work beyond their tenure. The cleric also prayed for God to ease the burdens and responsibilities borne by traditional rulers across Northern Nigeria, particularly their efforts to secure peace and stability in their communities. item.title: The Cross that killed, the Cross that kills
item.description: By Fada Oluoma Sometimes last year i went to purchase a crucifix for my church at the popular St Cecelia’s sacramental shop in Wuse Zone 2. I was accompanied by my catechist and one other parishioner. We had a short argument on what size to buy. I chose a small one, the catechist argued that we should buy a much bigger one that will occupy up to 80 percent of the space reserved for it. I refused and used my veto power to get the small one. Back then, I wasn’t even thinking about the possibility of a crucifix falling from it’s position and unaliving a priest or anyone in the church. I was driven more by modesty or simplicity. I believe in keeping things as simple as possible. The cross i chose, though small is still very visible to anyone from any corner of that church. I didn’t see the need for a bigger one. The chilling death of a priest by a wooden cross that fell on him gives me more reason to justify my choice retroactively. Both cynics and critics have taken a dig at the Catholic faith over a cross killing a priest in church. To them, it is a caricature of our belief in a good and powerful God. To some other Christians, it is a punishment against idolatry, a sin they accuse Catholic Church of because of images. To some Catholics, it is ominous and a sucker punch. Trying to explain away the deep and uncomfortable contradictions and pains this event causes would be simplistic and probably dishonest, perhaps delusional. We must accept and grapple with the scruples without losing our faith in God. However, the most important thing about it are the lessons we must learn. They are as follows: Death can occur anywhere and any time. People have been killed in churches and other sacred places. Prayer is sacred. Yet, if you pray in a church or grotto with mosquitoes, they are gonna bite and cause you malaria if you don’t take precaution and protect yourself. The prayer you are saying won’t protect you from their bite, unless God decides to use your case as miracle. In churches, safety measures cannot be sacrificed for any pious oestentation, aestetics or expression. A giant crucifix hung on any church must be done in such a way that it will never accidentally fall on anyone. If this safety concern cannot be guaranteed by engineering, a small and lighter one that poses no threat to life could be placed instead. It’s most likely that signs of cracks on the wall where that crucifix was hung had begun showing but people didn’t take notice. There is a difference between the cross that killed the priest and the cross on which Jesus Christ died. It wasn’t that cross that killed Jesus Christ. It was on that cross that Jesus died. The difference between the two is too deep and clear to be mistaken. The cross of Jesus Christ still kills, yes. It kills our egos, lusts, selfishness, fear, doubts, carnal appetites, vices. item.title: Organisers reveals how Kane edged Mbappe to Ballon d’Or win
item.description: Harry Kane won the Ballon d’Or by the smallest margin under its current voting system when he edged Kylian Mbappe by 28 points, France Football which runs the awards, revealed on Friday. The magazine published a breakdown of the votes in its Friday edition. Bayern Munich’s Kane, the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001, received 40 first-place votes from the 100 jurors and a total of 1,055 points. France captain Mbappe of Real Madrid was placed first 23 times and finished with 1,027 points. The previous smallest margin was 41 when Rodri, then of Manchester City, edged another Real player Vinicius Junior by 41 points in 2024. Last season, Paris Saint-Germain forward Ousmane Dembele totalled 1,380 points as he finished 321 points ahead of Lamine Yamal of Barcelona. This summer, Yamal won a World Cup with Spain but he finished third in the voting on 881 points, 174 behind Kane. The Ballon d’Or is awarded following a vote by journalists (one per country) representing the top 100 nations in the FIFA rankings for men, and the top 50 for women. item.title: Debt Worse Than Leprosy, Destroys Generations, Says Obasanjo
item.description: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his position on borrowing, declaring that debt is worse than leprosy because it destroys generations. He stated this while speaking at a symposium, a public forum focused on leveraging Artificial Intelligence to solve grassroots problems and accelerate national development in Abeokuta, Ogun State. Tinubu had said in April that borrowing should not be viewed negatively, insisting that the government would borrow when necessary, provided it could repay the loans. President Bola Tinubu (Photo: X@aonanuga1956) But Obasanjo disagreed, describing such a position as absolute nonsense. The former president also questioned Nigeria’s economic performance, recalling that when he established his farm 47 years ago, the naira exchanged at ₦1 to $1 and 85 cents. He challenged the country’s leadership to explain the naira’s depreciation to about ₦1,500 to a dollar, questioning what Nigeria had achieved over the decades. Meanwhile, the guest speaker, historian and public policy scholar, Umar Ardo, has warned that artificial intelligence could deepen Africa’s dependence on foreign powers if the continent fails to control its technology and digital infrastructure. Ardo warned that without investments in chip fabrication, data centres, African-owned datasets and continental cooperation, artificial intelligence could become another tool for managing Africa rather than empowering the continent to determine its own future. Amid criticism, President Tinubu on Thursday defended his administration’s plan to take more foreign loans , arguing that Nigeria needs long-term investment in infrastructure to achieve its ambition of becoming a $1 trillion economy by 2030. The President said the proposed loans would be used to build roads, improve electricity supply, upgrade ports and fund other projects that would create jobs, grow businesses and provide opportunities for future generations. In a statement titled “From Reforms to Delivery: Our Infrastructure Investment and Growth Strategy,” Tinubu said the focus should be on what the borrowed money would achieve rather than how much the government was borrowing. “The key question is not how much we borrow, but what we build, the value we create and the future we leave behind,” he said. He listed the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid improvements and upgrades to major commercial ports in Lagos among the projects the government plans to fund. He said the projects, alongside investments in healthcare, education and vocational training, would connect economic regions, reduce the cost of transporting goods, support farming and industries, and attract private investors. The President said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway alone could reduce transport costs along its route by 15 to 20 per cent and add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) through increased trade, tourism

item.title: Fani-Kayode Presents Letters Of Credence, Assumes Duties As High Commissioner In South Africa
item.description: A former Minister of Aviation, Femi Fani-Kayode, has formally presented copies of his Letters of Credence to the Deputy Director-General, Public Diplomacy, and Acting Chief of State Protocol, Mr Clayson Monyela, at the South African Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO). The presentation on Friday marked an important diplomatic milestone, signifying the formal commencement of Fani-Kayode’s diplomatic functions and his assumption of duties as Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa with effect from October 30, 2026. This photo shows Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode (centre), meeting with South African officials on October 30, 2026. Following the presentation, Fani-Kayode also met with the Deputy Director-General of DIRCO in his office, as part of his initial diplomatic engagements with senior South African government officials. The presentation of copies of his Letters of Credence precedes the ceremonial presentation of his Letters of Credence to South Africa’s President Cyril Ramaphosa, which will take place in a few days. This photo shows Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode (left), presenting his Letters of Credence on October 30, 2026. In a statement dated October 28, the Department of International Relations and Cooperation of the Republic of South Africa explained that the Minister of International Relations and Cooperation had approved a policy change in terms of Article 13 (1) of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961, to replace the current practice where a Head of Mission-Designate would have to present the original Letters of Credence to the President before being considered as having taken up their functions in the receiving state. “The Department wishes to confirm that once the Head of Mission-Designate has submitted the copies of the Letters of Credence to the Chief of State Protocol, the said Head of Mission-Designate is considered to have taken up his / her position as Head of Mission,” the statement read in part. “The Department wishes to furthermore confirm that the original Letters of Credence will still be handed over to the President at the next Credentials Ceremony on a date and time to be communicated. The Department of International Relations and Cooperation of the Republic of South Africa avails itself of this opportunity to renew to the High Commission of the Federal Republic of Nigeria the assurances of its highest consideration.” The post Fani-Kayode Presents Letters Of Credence, Assumes Duties As High Commissioner In South Africa appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Nigeria, Russia Review 1967 Bilateral Air Services Agreement
item.description: Nigeria on Friday met with the Russian Federation on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, Russia, as both countries move to strengthen aviation relations and expand cooperation in the air transport sector. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, led Nigeria’s delegation to a high-level bilateral meeting. At the meeting, the Nigerian delegation, led by Keyamo, held discussions with Dmitry Stanislavovich Zverev, who is the State Secretary and Deputy Minister of Transport of the Russian Federation, on the need to modernise the existing framework governing air services between the two countries. A major outcome of the meeting was the resolution by both sides to renegotiate the Bilateral Air Services Agreement (BASA) between Nigeria and Russia, which dates back to 1967, with a view to establishing a new agreement that reflects contemporary developments and emerging opportunities in international aviation. The meeting centred on the need to modernise the existing framework governing air services between the two countries. According to a statement by the aviation ministry, both countries agreed on a six-month timeline to conclude the negotiations and sign the new agreement in Saint Petersburg, Russia, in April 2027. To facilitate the process, the two sides have constituted their respective negotiating teams to commence work immediately and ensure that the agreed timeline is met. “The proposed agreement is expected to provide an updated framework for bilateral air transport relations and create opportunities for enhanced connectivity, closer institutional collaboration and mutually beneficial engagement between the aviation sectors of both countries,” the statement signed by the minister’s Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Tunde Moshood. The Nigerian delegation included the Director-General of the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), Capt. Chris Najomo; the Registrar of the Nigerian College of Aviation Technology (NCAT), Dr. Danjuma Adamu Ismaila, as well as directors from the Federal Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development and the NCAA. “Beyond the review of the existing air services agreement, the meeting also explored other potential areas of cooperation between Nigeria and Russia,” the statement disclosed. It added that both parties expressed their commitment to examining the opportunities in the coming months, with a view to deepening bilateral relations and identifying areas of shared interest in aviation and related sectors.
